$comment: Divergences introduced by the implementation, beyond the reconstructed reference. DIV-001..DIV-009 are normative and live in the frozen corpus register (docs/corpus/33_DIVERGENCE_REGISTER.md); they are listed here read-only so a spec can reference either range and the gate can check it. Constitution Article X: a change that alters recovered behavior preserves the governing test or introduces an explicit DIV with rationale and a parity note.

live_divergences.title: Withhold control-shaped tokens in a recovered region instead of narrating them
live_divergences.decision: In a narration region that contains a registered action, every `key=value` token is withheld from the narration channel and recorded on the recovered command (declared key or not), rather than being spoken when it falls outside the contiguous kwargs run.
live_divergences.rationale: The reconstructed reference implementation recovers a bare command by consuming contiguous assignments, then narrates everything after the first non-assignment token. For `whiteboard.text id=t text=If exactly one split size=lg` that narrates `exactly one split size=lg`, putting an assignment into the spoken channel. Constitution Article V is explicit that control-shaped text must never become narration, and Article I forbids raw producer output reaching a public effect. The word-based rule cannot locate the boundary between a multi-word value and resumed narration, so the boundary is not trusted: anything shaped like an assignment is withheld.
live_divergences.parity_note: Diverges from docs/corpus/harness/stagehand-conformance.mjs case A-002 only in the disposition of tokens *after* the recovered command's kwargs run. A-002's assertions (`commands[0].action === 'avatar.move'`, `text === 'Hello student'`) still hold: the trailing narration there contains no assignment. Recorded and surfaced on the recovered command rather than dropped, so the registry reports `Unknown keyword argument` and the token stays visible in the production channel instead of vanishing (Article XII).

live_divergences.title: Adopt the Virtual Classroom whiteboard superset for the six actions both hosts declare
live_divergences.decision: For whiteboard.show/hide/clear/text/line/box the SDK follows the pinned Virtual Classroom contracts, not Clio's. Concretely: `hide` occludes and preserves content (Clio's ends the beat and wipes marks); `id` is required rather than optional on the creating actions; `content_ref`, `region`, and `conceal` are accepted; `conceal`/`size`/`style` enum constraints and the x/y/x1..y2/stroke numeric constraints are enforced; and `settleMs` is declared per action.
live_divergences.rationale: The pinned Virtual Classroom source states the divergence itself: 'Deliberate divergence from Clio, where `whiteboard.hide` wipes marks. In a classroom the projector occludes the board; it does not end its presentation.' Clio's surface list cannot express the difference — its data says only 'Hide the full-screen whiteboard surface' — so a reconstruction that compressed both hosts into one behavior string had to pick one, and picking Clio's destroys a lesson's work. Adopting the superset is the choice the corpus's own FEAT-012 intent implies ('a reusable screen-space explanatory canvas' whose content survives being hidden), and it is recorded rather than left implicit.
live_divergences.parity_note: Diverges from the Clio surfaces SURF-034..039 as declared in their own source. The VC contracts are the parity target, and docs/evidence/virtual-classroom-whiteboard.json records both sides so the difference is auditable. A Clio-behavior consumer that relied on `hide` wiping a board must call `whiteboard.clear` instead; that is the one behavioural change with a migration cost, and it is the change that makes content survivable. TEST-204 asserts the distinction and would fail if `hide` were re-implemented as `clear`.
